entries.source: It is often enough for most applications but some others need that the original 3D dimension be kept in UV space. In those cases islands are usually smaller or bigger than a UV tile which has 1x1 dimension.		   The parameters present in that feature allow you to adapt the dimension of the UV tile to its content. Which can give a better workflow in some cases.

Notice that the packing algorithm will distribute the islands into the available or active tiles when pressing 'P'. If you don't want the island by distributed into the available tiles, select the islands before pressing 'P'. Selected islands will be transformed and each of them will remain in their current tile
Note: It's worth noting that double clicking on a island of a group will select all group content.
Note: It's worth noting that double clicking on a island of a group will select all the trim content.
Use this when you want to get rid of some bad cuts or want to avoid a reset

'Isolate' term that appears in the following means the action to hide others islands and let visible the 'isolated' ones. It is a very convenient feature when dealing with meshes that are segmented in a lot islands. Pressing 'I' hover an island will isolate it, pressing 'Y' will unhide all of them. The 'Auto' isolate feature will isolate islands that have at least one edge selected.
- 'Lock' will lock them, preventing to be packed, so the new elements coming from the group will be packed around them.
- 'Repack' will pack these element along with the elements coming from the groups.
- 'Selection' uses the first selected island as source/reference and the selection set as candidate set.
- 'Straight' mode will enable Rizom to process geometrically identical islands with the same normal orientation only.
- 'Symmetric' will process islands which share the same topology and have inverted normal orientation including symmetric parts.
- Absolute Stretch (RS Only): Polygon color based on the polygon's stretch (UV polygon's area divided by the 3D polygon's area)
- Auto: Primitive behind polygons will be selected only if polygon display is disabled.
- Closed: The tile is fully closed, preventing islands from crossing the borders.
- Closest will potentially shrink or grow your primitives when fitting them to the grid, as they will be set to fit the grid closest to them
- Color ID Map : Island color defined by user, to be used in UV Stamp Exports (see File Exporter Dialog)
- Direction: Primitive behind polygons will be selected depending if the selection region is defined from left-to-right or right-to-left.

- Distortion : Polygon color based on the polygon's normalized stretch. The normalization use the average of the island's stretch (UV polygon's area over 3D polygon's area, divided by the average of the island's stretch)
- Larger will potentially enlarge your primitives when fitting them to the grid
- Material ID : Polygon color from the file's material ID
- Multi: The flipping will be applied independently each primitive groups or by island.
- Open Right : Islands can cross the right side of the tile, expanding the layout from left to right.
- Open Top & Left : Islands can cross the top and left sides of the tile, and the layout of islands will follow the tile's aspect ratio.
- Open Top : Islands can cross the top side of the tile, expanding the layout from bottom to top.
- Select Through Polygons: Primitives behind polygons will be selected.
- Select Visible: Only visible primitives will be selected.
- Single: The flipping will be applied to the global selection set like it would be a single part.
- Smaller will potentially shrink your primitives when fitting them to the grid.
- Texel Density : Polygon color based on the texel density
- Topology : Polygon color from vertex, edge and polygon count, helps to identify islands borders.
-Use 'Full' to let the island scale down to fit in the available space.
-Use 'Full' to let the island scale up to fill all the available space.
1. Pressing the 'TAB' key, then move the Gizmo's anchors, or

1:1 Scale$$Rescales island (s) to their original and absolute 3D space dimensions to ensure they occupy the same space in both 3D and UV-space. (On selected islands, or all islands if none selected. Any hidden islands are ignored)
1:1 Uniform Scale$$Rescale Uniformly Island(s) so that island's average UV area match(es) the 3D area (on selected islands, or on all islands if none selected)
2. Pressing the 'SPACE' key, drag the mouse while pressing the left or middle or right button, or
3. Changing directly the values in the controllers (you can multiply/divide/add/subtract current values by others, mathematic expressions are interpreted).
Across Seams$$Propagate the selection across the seams.
Activate Link gaps to link the mesh's gaps using path of edges (recommended especially for meshes that come from photogrammetry).
Activate Select handle to remove higher topologies genus automatically (recommended in most cases).

Activate the Size Limiter when you get too much long/bigger islands comparatively to the others. Long islands can make the packing unable to utilize efficiently the UV area since they form an island stack not square.

Activate the Smooth when dealing with scanned meshes that have many small useless details that you don't want to be separated from the rest of the mesh. Note that smooth influence can be controlled using the protect/attract map.

Activate the Stretch Control if you want to remove excessive stretching and angle distortion that remains after the main seam tool algorithm segmentation. The downside of that option is it creates more cut, sometimes over segmentation.
Add Color to Palette$$Add current color to palette
Add$$Insert the selected islands or group into the underlying existing group.
Adjusts the scale of UV islands to maintain an average texel density across all islands.
Align Island Horizontally to Selection$$Align island(s) horizontally using what is selected.
Align Island Vertically to Selection$$Align island(s) vertically using what is selected.

Align Matching Islands to Edge$$Aligns (cut) island(s) to matching edges. This means that if you cut an island in two, and you select one edge, clicking this button will bring the opposite island's matching edge close to the selected one. This only works on the edges on the boundaries of an island, and not inside an island
Align to Grid Center$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Horizontal Center$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Left$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Low Left$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Low Right$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Low$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Right$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Up Left$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Up Right$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Up$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align to Grid Vertical Center$$Align selection to the selected grid or tile or trim
Align UV to 3D: orient so that their UV space axis aligns to the 3D Space axis.

All islands in a group that is in stack mode will no been repacked / transformed even if they are selected. However, the group stack itself can be transformed and the contained islands will be moved using the same transformation applied to the group. It is like if they where in a box, the box move and bring what it contains.

An image of a trimsheet might look like a grid or collage containing various distinct, rectangular sections. Each section would have a different texture or pattern such as metallic surfaces, rivets, grilles, and other industrial motifs. The textures are usually aligned and designed to seamlessly tile across a surface. The overall appearance is akin to a patchwork of textures, each clearly defined within its own borders, allowing for easy mapping onto 3D surfaces.
Apply Color to Selection$$Apply color to island selection
Apply Texel Density Uniformly$$Once you've picked or set your Texel Density, clicking the Set Density Uniformly icon uniformly scales selection to the average of the specified density.
Apply Texel Density$Shift-Q$Once you've picked or set your Texel Density, clicking the Apply Density icon scales selection to the specified texel density.
Area Tool Mode Polyline$$RMB to add point, DRMB to finish, RMB to cancel, MMB to remove last point.
As with Unwrap and Optimize, the packing will be applied to selected islands and groups or, if no selection is made, on all visible islands.

Aspect Ratio Influence$$To control the influence of the aspect ratio, adjust the setting accordingly: set it to 0 to disregard the aspect ratio entirely, focusing solely on the area; set it to 1 to consider only the aspect ratio.

At the heart of this panel is the Similarity slider, your go - to tool for setting the criteria of similarity. By adjusting this slider, you define the level of resemblance required between islands or elements for the topology updates to be transferred.This ensures a seamless and efficient workflow, allowing for precision and consistency in your UV mapping tasks.
Auto Fit: Adapt to available space
Auto Isolate Island$Shift-Alt-H$Enable/Disable automatic islands isolation. When on, islands which haven't any edge selected will be automatically hidden.
Auto Seams$$Locks the Auto Seams panel to the right panel docker.
Auto Seams$$The Auto Seams panel contains advanced algorithms to select automatically some edges of the visible islands set that would be good candidate to serve to cut and segment your islands.
Auto: The range is determined automatically using the min and max texel density value on all visible islands
Automatic: orient horizontally or vertically before being positioned. If the island is almost horizontal, it will become perfectly horizontal, same for the vertical case.
Automatically assigns UV islands to trims based on their size. This ensures the smallest islands are placed on the smallest trims and the largest islands on the largest trims.

Average Normal Projection$Alt-U$Project 3D geometry using the average normal of each islands or each isolated group of selected primitives. Applied on selection if non-empty or on everything in the contrary case.
Avoid Triangle Flips$$When set to active, running Unfold and Optimize avoid the creation of triangle flips. PLEASE NOTE: This can significantly increase the unwrapping or optimizing calculation time.
Base Scale$$Base scale of the islands to be packed
Best Fit$$When keep proportion is on, the fitting axis will be chosen so that the islands do not cross their trim limits
Border Intersection$$When active, Unfold and Optimize avoid creation of self border intersections. PLEASE NOTE: This can significantly increase the unwrapping or optimizing calculation time.
Bounding Box Based Transform Anchoring$$Define the transformation pivot using the selection bounding box control points.
Box Mode On$$The outline of the island/group is replaced by a bounding- or control box while packing.
Box Projection$$Project 3D geometry on the 6 faces of a cube. Tip: use AutoSeam Box Tool to well prepare the cut of the object before.
Box X+Y+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X+ and Y+
Box X+Y-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X+ and Y-
Box X+Z+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X+ and Z+
Box X+Z-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X+ and Z-
Box X-Y+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X- and Y+
Box X-Y-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X- and Y-
Box X-Z+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X- and Z+
Box X-Z-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces X- and Z-
Box Y+Z+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces Y+ and Z+
Box Y+Z-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces Y+ and Z-
Box Y-Z+$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces Y- and Z+
Box Y-Z-$$Auto Select Box will select the edge intersecting virtual box faces Y- and Z-
Box$$Select edges using the Box algorithm. Each island are projected on 6 orthogonal planes and form several polygon groups. All polygon groups borders are then selected.
Brush Size$$Brush size in painting mode.
Bug Report...$$Launch browser to the official RizomUV support page...
Center Selection$F$Center View on the selection set.
Clear Hinge$$Remove the hinge constraint on selected vertexes
Color ID Map Current Color$$Color used when applying color to island in color ID map mode.

Color ID Map Editor$$The color ID map editor allows you to define by island colors. To use it, switch to island selection mode (F4), then select some islands and apply some colors using the provided tools.
Color Map Mode$$- Disabled: No color map display in viewport

Color Map$$The Color Map is an effective tool that enables users to visualize specific data types through the use of colors and histograms, and to select primitives that fall within a designated value range.
Color Palette$$Colors that can be used to define the ColorID Map
ColorID From Island Groups$$Assigns colorID using island group to visible or selected islands
ColorID From MaterialID$$Assigns colorID using file's material ID to visible or selected islands
Constrain Edge(s) Aligned$$Constrain the selected edges to be aligned when unfolding and optimizing. You need to update optimize to see the effects.
Constrain Edge(s) Horizontally$Alt-T$Constrain the selected edges to be horizontal when unfolding and optimizing. You need to update optimize to see the effects.
Constrain Edge(s) Vertically$Alt-V$Constrain the selected edges to be vertical when unfolding and optimizing. You need to update optimize to see the effects.
Contextual Help$$Locks the Contextual Help panel to the right panel docker.
Contextual Help$$The contextual help panel display some tips and the current mouse and keyboard interaction depending on the primitive selection mode and the edit tool mode.
Control Customizer$$Control Customizer allows you to customize your mouse and keyboard interaction with RizomUV
Control Customizer...$$Open the keyboard and mouse customizer dialog
Copy$$Copies the selected UV set data in the current set. This means you can copy full layouts between channels for further refinement.
Create Group Stack$$Create a new stack mode group using the current island/group selection.
Create Rigid Group$$Create a new rigid group using the current island/group selection. When packed the content of a rigid group is rescaled to fit the group's shape.

Create some trims using the "Create" button. You can repeat the process using Repeat (Alt-R) until you have enough trims to cover the UV tile. Once your trim layout is done, you may want to prevent your trims from being reshaped by mistake. If so enable the "Lock Trims Shapes" button, this will prevent the trims from being selected by the marquee selection tool.
Create$$Creates a new UV set in the list.
Create...$$Create a new tag and assign it to the selection
Curved Mode$$Extract curved shapes like cylinders, spheres, and cones

Cut and Unwrap$$Auto Seams tool will cut then flatten the processed geometry after the edges being selected. This option makes the computation of the auto segmentation and the unfolding far more slower but gives better quality.
Cut$C$Use in edge, polygon mode to create seams on the mesh. If the selection is empty, the edge located under the mouse pointer will be cut.
Cut, Unwrap, Pack$$Auto Seams tool will pack the processed islands after the edges being selected, island cut then flattened.
Define S0's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 0.
Define S1's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 1.
Define S2's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 2.
Define S3's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 3.
Define S4's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 4.
Define S5's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 5.
Define S6's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 6.
Define S7's Path...$$Define the file path of the script 7.
Delete$$Deletes the selected UV set from the list.
Denormalize$$Rescale the tile and its content so that the tile ratio match the User Texture's ratio.

Density$F8$Switch to edit mode density multiplier map. Once edited, a value of the density multiplier different from zero will change the UV polygon's area after running optimize. Packing will also take account the density multiplier map by giving island different scales, and hotspot will do as well.

Density: Switch to edit mode density multiplier map. Once edited, a value of the density multiplier different from zero will change the UV polygon's area after running optimize. Packing will also take account the density multiplier map by giving island different scales, and hotspot will do as well.
Deselect All$$Deselect all trims, keeping others elements such as islands, groups and tiles in their current selection state.
Deselect$$Deselect islands and groups that have the selected tags
Details Remover Map Controlled$$The protect/attract map will be used to determine the zones to protect from being selected. Red zones will prevents the edges to be selected.
Details Remover Off$$Details will be selected.
Details Remover On$$Small details will tend to be ignored.
Detect Radial$$When active, radial shaped islands will be placed in trims tagged as radial if any.
Display Border Edges Only$$The orientation map mode will display only the border edges.
Display Tile ID Type$$Convention used to display the tile id

Distortion Energy Based Mode$$If enabled, Unfold and Optimize features stops when the distortion energy becomes sufficiently low or stagnates. If disabled, Unfold and Optimize stop when the specified Iteration Count is reached. It's worth noting that if you're not sure about your iterations, you should turn this back on, as it's the better in 99% of unwrapping cases. If you are dealing with dense geometry and the Auto mode takes ages to compute, or inversely does nothing, use the spinners of the manual mode.
Distribute Bottom$$Distributes your selection vertically to the bottom.
Distribute Center Horizontally$$Distributes your selection to a common horizontal center.
Distribute Center Vertically$$Distributes your selection to a common vertical center.

Distribute Groups Connected Primitive Sets$$Distributes features groups connected set of primitives. Turn this on especially when you are in Vertex Mode and want your vertices to move uniformly. When disabled, each vertex will be moved independently.
Distribute Left$$Distributes your selection horizontally to the left
Distribute Right$$Distributes your selection horizontally to the right.
Distribute Space Horizontally$$Distributes your selection on a horizontally spaced axis.

Distribute Space Mode$$Available mode distributes evenly the available space between selected items. Real mode distributes the specified space in real unit between items. Pixel mode distributes the specified space in pixel unit between items.
Distribute Space Pixel Interval Value$$Space put between items in pixel unit
Distribute Space Real Interval Value$$Space put between items in real value unit
Distribute Space Vertically$$Distributes your selection on a vertically spaced axis.
Distribute Top$$Distributes your selection vertically to the top
Distribute$$Distribute move all active islands (or groups) currently outside the tile grid into active tiles before packing operation.
Download...$$Launch browser to the official RizomUV downloading page...
Drag: Switch to edit mode drag
Dynamic Color Palette$$The dynamic color palette shows currently used color among all the island set
Edge Loop$$This panel defines how you want the Edge Loop tool to behave, it will appear when you select working in Edge mode by clicking the icon, the menu or using the F2 key.
Edge$F2$Lets you select and work at edge level
Edit S0$$Open script 0 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S1$$Open script 1 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S2$$Open script 2 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S3$$Open script 3 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S4$$Open script 4 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S5$$Open script 5 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S6$$Open script 6 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit S7$$Open script 7 for edition in the user-defined editor.
Edit Toolbar$$The Edit ToolBar contains selectors to change the principal RizomUV edition modes
Efficient: Focuses on fast computation. Prioritizes quick packing over precise padding or alignment. Suitable for rapid iterations and previews.

Elastic$$When activated, the selection will exhibit elastic properties, similar to those of a rubber band. Conversely, if it is not enabled, it will mimic the behavior of modeling clay. To put it another way, when the feature is turned on, the island's deformation will revert to its original unfolded state before adapting to the user's constraints.

Enable curved to select revolution or curved shapes. The more the angle is high, the more you will select polygons. Try small values before and augment the value until you get enough selected polygons.
Enable Mouse Wheel$$Enable or disable the mouse wheel. Magic mouse user for example may disable this option.
Enable planar to select planar shapes. The more the angle is high, the more you will select polygons. Try small values before and augment the value until you get enough selected polygons.

Enable Proportional Falloff Edit$$Enable Soft Selection for Transforms. When activated, the transformations will by softly propagated to the connected primitives around a distance set by "Falloff", with an attenuation curve: The "Falloff Profile".
Enable Snapping$$Enable snapping using current snapping settings

Enable the soft selection mode, then select some points / edges / polygons, then transform them using the available transforms tools (see the Transform Panel for that) then primitives around the selection will be moved as well according to their distance to the selection set.
Enable$$Check stretching and add enough cuts to ensure no flips and no overlaps once the mesh will be unfolded as a post process.

Enable/Disable Pin Map Primitive For Proportional Mode$$Enable/Disable "Pin Map" for Proportional Edit. When enabled, the more the vertexes are dark the less they will be transformed. Disabling it allows you to displace the pinned primitives without having to clear the Pin map.
Enable/Disable$Alt-S$Enable/Disable symmetry mode for selection, unfolding and edition
Equalize: Resizes the islands so their texel density will match the average texel density of the selected, or currently transformed islands.
Existing$$If there is existing islands in the tiles,

Export Layout...$$Export trims from an SVG file. All trims in the layout will be transformed into rectangular shapes for export to the SVG file. Attributes such as color, Fit Axis, tags, and other properties will also be included in the shape's description
Falloff Curve$$Set the proportional editing falloff curve type.
Falloff Distance to Screen Space Mode$$Set the proportional falloff distance to screen space mode. When enabled, the unity of "Falloff" is relative to the viewport's space, otherwise to world space
Falloff Distance$$Set the transform editing falloff distance.
Feat Request...$$Launch browser to the official RizomUV support page...

Fill Gaps$$Polygon count of a given polygon group under which it will be systematically selected whatever the polygon orientation. Increment the value if you get sparse small groups of unselected polygon.

Fill Holes$$When active, Unfold and Optimize patch the mesh's holes by adding invisible, temporary polygons to the model, so when an unwrap or optimize occurs, it prevents the hole from collapsing on various types of unwraps. Use this on eyes, mouths, nostrils, clothing and hard edge openings like the hole on top of a tank or non-square windows.
Filling Direction$$Filling direction when distributing selected groups into the grid.
Filter Islands$$This panel consists of tools specifically created to select sets of islands based on the parameters you define.
Finally, please note that when using Weld in Edge Mode, the edges will move differently in UV space if you select only a side or both sides of the seams.
Fit to Grid Add Margin$$Add a margin between the element and the grid. The size of the margin is determined by the margin in the Layout Panel.
Fit to Grid Grouping Mode$$Define if the selection will be segmented into independent groups or processed as a single tied element, or processed independently vertex by vertex.
Fit U and V$$Fits the bounding box of your selected primitives to the grid. This option will scale U and V direction independently
Fit U Proportionally$$Fits the bounding box's U size of your selected primitives to the grid's U size. This option will scale in both direction while keeping original proportions of the selection.

Fit U V Proportionally$$Best fits the bounding box's V or U size of your selected primitives to the U or V dimension of the grid. This option will scale in both direction while keeping original proportions of the selection.
Fit U$$Fits the bounding box of your selected primitives to the grid. This option will scale in the U direction and translate in the V direction following the alignment mode
Fit UV Tile and add Margin$$Fit UV Tile to the current selection adding a margin (margin value from pack and layout panel).
Fit UV Tile to Origin and add Margin$$Move the mesh to the origin then fit the the UV tile to the current selection. A margin will be added (the margin value come from layout panel).
Fit V Proportionally$$Fits the bounding box's U size of your selected primitives to the grid's U size. This option will scale in both direction while keeping original proportions of the selection.
Fit V$$Fits the bounding box of your selected primitives to the grid. This option will scale in the V direction and translate in the U direction following the alignment mode
Fit$Alt-B$Rescale selected islands to fit the UV Square (without deforming them)
Flip Axis Mode$$- Tile: The flipping axis will be determined by the tile geometry that contains the current selection.
Flip Horizontal Left$$Flip the selection horizontally using the left side of the bounding box as flip axis
Flip Horizontal Right$$Flip the selection horizontally using the right side of the bounding box as flip axis
Flip Vertical Bottom$$Flip the selection vertically using the bottom side of the bounding box as flip axis
Flip Vertical Top$$Flip the selection vertically using the top side of the bounding box as flip axis
Follow: Resize the islands so that their texel density will match the average texel density of islands already inside the tile, that are non-selected and non-locked.
For other modes, use the selector on the left side of the color map to choose the data type you wish to display. You can then select primitives by dragging the mouse across the color map.
Force$$High values will segment more so the islands will be unfolded with less distortion. Low values will segment less but the cut will generate more distortion.
Free Selection Border$$When active, Unfold and Optimize will not block the vertexes that are on the selection set border so that they can freely move.

Geometric$$This option is especially handy for complex, triangulated mesh. When active, it will try to find a straight selection of edges, creating a straight path where possible. It will do this even where a plethora of n-gons are connected - which will not happen if this mode is disabled.
Group Opacity$$Opacity of the group' background in viewport display
Group Overlapped$Shift-Ctrl-G$Detect overlapped island sets and create groups for all of them.
Group$G$Create a new elastic group using the current island/group selection. An elastic groups adapt its shape to the size of its content.
Groups$$Groups allow you to gather set of island. Note that some features are also available for tiles too.
Handles$$Select all handles of the mesh using path of edges, or seams.
Hide Selected/Hovered Island(s)$H$Hide selected islands or the island under the mouse.
High Force$$High number of cuts, low distortion

Hinge$$Make the selected vertex(es) become hinge(s). PLEASE NOTE: This has only an influence if the hinge is located between two consecutive edges that have Edge Aligned Constraints. You need to update optimize to see the effects.
Horizontal Tile Size$$Set UV tile horizontal size
Horizontal Tiles$$Number of rows of the grid tile.
Horizontal: orient horizontally before being positioned.
Horizontalize$Shift-H$Aligns selected edges or points on a horizontal axis

Hotspot Mapping$S$Transform selected islands and groups to fit the available Trims, based on their geometry. Please note that you can hover over an island at any time and press 'S' to hotspot it, even when you're in a mode other than the island selection mode.

Hotspot$$The "hotspotting" feature in RizomUV automates the placement of UV islands onto trims by matching them based on area, aspect ratio, and tags.This process ensures appropriate scaling and thematic consistency of textures on 3D models.

If you have some islands that are not similar, but you want them to keep their position / rotation / scale relatively to other islands of the group, you can use the Group Stack button. The islands will keep their current transformation and be grouped in a Group Stack.

If you have some islands that are similar (i.e same topology and same shape in 3D), they are good candidate to be stacked in the diffuse map. You can use Stack & Group Stack button for them. It will stack the similar islands over each other, then put them in a new Group Stack.
In addition, there are two additional Weld modes :
In all primitive selection modes (point/edge/polygons/island), pressing the 'D' key + mouse buttons will transform the island which is under the mouse pointer.
In case of noisy meshes, adding some smooth iterations will give you cleaner polygon selection sets

Intersection Gap$$The minimal distance between where the island's borders intersect with themselves, in pixels or real (UV) units, depending on your Layout Panel's settings. WARNING, keep low values like 1 or 2 pixels maximum, otherwise you take the risk to block Optimize and Unfold features
Invert Map$$Will invert the current map (on selected islands, or all islands if none selected)
Invert Mouse Wheel$$Invert mouse wheel effect on zoom
Invert Mouse Zoom Drag Direction$$Invert mouse zoom drag direction
Island and Groups$F4$Lets you select and work with islands, groups, tiles and trims
Island Count Manual$$Mosaic segmentation will not automatically determines the island count for each island to segment but use the specified value.
Island Count$$Number of parts in which each island must be segmented into.

Island Groups can be simply used to classify some of your islands because you want to isolate them from the rest of the whole mesh model, or they can be used to specify to the packing algorithm that you want them placed together in the UV space. To create a group, select some islands then press 'G'.
Island Scaling Factor$$Scaling factor applied to island(s) at packing stage.

Island Visibility$$Island visibility controls the visibility of the islands in the viewport but also determines which islands will be processed by the algorithms. As a general rule hidden islands will not be processed. However hidden islands will be saved into files even if they are not visible in the viewport.
Islands and Tile Uniform Scale 1:1$$Rescale Uniformly Island(s) and Tiles so that island's average UV area match(es) the 3D area (on selected islands, or on all islands if none selected)

Iteration Count$$The number of iterations plays a crucial role when deforming a mesh. A higher number of iterations tends to yield more accurate and refined results; however, it also results in increased computation time, leading to slower performance.
Keep current: Islands will not be re-oriented before being positioned.
Keep Metric$$When active, Optimize resizes the processed polygons so that their UV space area equals their 3D space area.
Keep Proportions$$Keep island proportions when fitting islands into trims.
Keep: Keep will not do anything to resize the islands being packed
Keeps the UV islands at their current scale without any adjustments.
Length Ratio$$Maximum allowed ratio of the bounding box length over the average of the maximum bounding box length of all islands. Low values create many cuts, high values create less cuts.
Limit Angle$$Stop the selection when the angle between to edges are superior to the angle defined by the slider.
Limit Count$$Limit the edge count to the edge loop selection tool.
Link Gaps$$Link all gaps and borders with path of edges, or seams.
Live Cut Mode$$Update unwrap mode after a cut or a weld action. Choose Disabled option for heavy as since it can slow down the responsiveness

Live Optimize$$Activate the Live Optimize engine. This engine aids in minimizing stretching by performing optimization iterations on islands as you manipulate them through rotation, scaling, translation, or various other operations such as dragging, spreading, and pinching.

Live Optimize$$The Live Optimize engine actively adjusts the vertices around your current selection of points, edges, or polygons to minimize distortion during transformation. IMPORTANT: To achieve meaningful results, it is essential to set pinning constraints on certain vertices beforehand. The engine operates by executing optimization iterations on the islands in real-time. However, exercise caution when working with dense meshes, as this feature demands substantial computational power, potentially leading to a decrease in viewport refresh rate.
Live Update$$Adjusting the parameters will instantly update the hotspot mapping in real time.

Load Layout...$$Load trims from an SVG file or an image file. This action will replace any existing trims. All rectangular shapes within file will be imported and transformed into trims. Additionally, trim colors, properties such as 'Trim fit Axis', and tags will be loaded if using a SVG file. This is especially pertinent if the file was previously exported by RizomUV.
Load recent file list items without UVs
Local Angle Visualization$$Colorize edges with a purple color when their adjacent polygons form an angle superior to the local angle limit.
Lock Layout$$Prevent trims to be moved, reshaped, or selected by the rectangle, lasso and circle tools.
Lock$L$Forbid island or group transformation for the packing algorithm.

Locked Shape$$Lock the group frame's shape but let it move, and also let the group content be packed. Islands and groups' size will be adjusted so that they can fit into the group's box if their scaling constrains allow it.
Low Force$$Low number of cuts, but will generate distortion
Magic Wand Gizmo Enable$$Enable the display of the magic wand angles at the mouse pointer location.

Magnet Weld$$Magnet Weld welds edges that are superposed, or in very close proximity to each other in UV Space - aka the 2D view. You control the distance at which they weld by adjusting the values in the Magnet Weld spinner.

Similar$$The 'Similar' toolset empowers you to apply actions consistently across islands that share identical topology. Now, you might wonder, what exactly is topology? In the realm of 3D modeling, topology refers to the arrangement of polygons that form the mesh. Here, arrangement implies the connectivity of polygons and/or edges that constitute the shape of the model. The influence of topology extends across various aspects of a 3D workflow, impacting more than just UV maps. It plays a crucial role in simplifying the texturing process or altering the shape of the model.

Similarity$$The slider controls the similarity parameters Rizom needs to process an island. If the slider is at 0, all topologically similar islands will be processed. Set to 1, Rizom will process islands of exact matching geometry (exactly identical islands). It's worth noting both topology and 3D coordinates (geometry) will be taken into consideration when Rizom compares islands for similarity under the hood.

Trimsheet$$A trimsheet is a type of texture atlas used primarily in video game development and real time graphics. It consists of a collection of repeated patterns, details, and surface textures that are arranged on a single image file. These are used to efficiently add complex details and textures to 3D models without the need for high polygon counts. Trimsheets are particularly useful in creating detailed and consistent textures for environments and objects while optimizing the workflow and resource usage.

Unwrap$$Whether you cut and unwrap as you go, or do all your cuts and then unwrap, at some point you are going to need to use the Unwrap panel. To use it, your island(s) need at least one UV- or hard seam. (a hard seam is a cut in your model, not your UVs). Once you hit U to unwrap, RizomUV calculates the flattest and most distortion-less unwrap possible. There are several ways you can press the U key to unwrap: Either press U to unwrap all visible and non-flat islands, or select some primitives then hit U, or mouse-over an island and hit U. Once flattened, you can run an Optimize via the O key, to get rid of even more distortion. Using Optimize follows the same rules as the U-key. Get to know the Unwrap panel and its shortcuts for fast and flat unwraps.

Update Similar$$Updates the seams and the UV coordinates of the similar islands provided that their similarity matches. It's worth noting that this is not the same as the Stack Similar function, as Update Similar as it left the islands at their current location rather than forming a stack.

Weld Island Cut$Shift-W$Weld Island Cuts will weld these back independently without welding across islands if an island on your model has been given several cuts. It will only weld the cuts on the selected or moused - over island.

Weld Islands$Ctrl-W$If you have cut your mesh into several islands, select both sides of the cut, then Weld Islands will weld these back together. Use this when you want to weld specific islands back together and/or want to avoid a reset.

Weld Self Island, which will weld edges on the same island only, and Weld Across Island (CTRL + W), which will not weld any edges but the ones bordering to other islands.
Weld$W$Welds selected edges, polygons, or islands. If the selection is empty, the edge or loop located under the mouse pointer, if any, will be welded.

When using the check board as a texture map, it is preferable to set values superior to 1. The more your mesh will contains smaller parts, the more greater values will be generally appropriate to see correctly the distortion.

When utilizing a UV mapping application like RizomUV, you engage with the mesh's edges to slice and fine-tune your UV map. The goal is to achieve a map that is as flat as possible, facilitating a smoother texturing experience. A model characterized by well-distributed quads significantly eases this process. Furthermore, when the model eventually undergoes triangulation by a game engine, this balanced topology ensures the generation of cleaner triangles.
Worth noting that only edges that have been previously cut can be welded.
You activate the edge loop feature by double-clicking on an edge.

You can also define the behavior of the Edge Loop when working in Edge Mode : You can set it to find the shortest path between two edges in opposite ends using the V-key or switch back to edge loop selection using the B-key.
You can cut or weld in Edge(F2), Polygon(F3), or Island Mode(F4)

You can obviously use classic transformation tools present in the Transform panel (F5 key) to place your islands, but the Fit & Align sub panel, present in the Misc Transform panel would certainly be a better option. Don't forget to set the "Match to" option to "Trim".

You may want to tag your islands and trims to ensure that only islands with the same tag are placed on the same trim. You can also tag trims as radial to ensure that only radial-shaped islands are placed on them.
Your model need to be cut and your islands flattened before using hotspot.
